env_strategy:
One environment is viable and recommended: a single uv project on Python 3.12, with the heavy families as optional dependency groups (core, ultralytics, rfdetr, hf) and lazy imports.

Reasons:
- All four sets resolve to one consistent set with wheels only (no source builds), with identical versions on 3.12 and 3.13. Adding rfdetr, supervision and transformers forces no downgrade of torch, numpy or ultralytics. rfdetr already requires transformers 5.x, so set D adds only timm and accelerate, and neither is required for Grounding DINO, OWLv2, SAM 2 or SAM 3.
- Packages cost almost no disk here. uv on this APFS volume uses link mode "clone" by default (stated in the installed uv 0.12.22 help text), and I confirmed it: libtorch_cpu.dylib in an existing environment sits on the same physical blocks as the copy in the uv cache. Pinned to cached versions, the lean set needs 0.03 MB of new download and the full set 3.1 MB.
- Splitting into several environments would save no disk and would add a second interpreter path, more bytecode and more ways to break. Model weights and RAM are the real constraints, not packages.

Conditions:
- Use Python 3.12, not 3.13 or 3.14. The cached torch, numpy, scipy, pillow and matplotlib wheels are cp312 builds; on 3.13 the full set costs 233 MB of download and 862 MB of disk instead of 3 MB and 11 MB.
- Keep exactly one OpenCV distribution. Use opencv-python (cached, 5.1.0.95) and drop opencv-python-headless from the core list, or use ultralytics-opencv-headless. Never both.
- Isolate heavy models at run time instead of by environment: load one model at a time and run inference in a worker subprocess so memory is returned when a run ends.
- A separate environment is only justified if an original research repository is added later (Meta's own sam2 or sam3 package, the original GroundingDINO repo with compiled ops). That is not needed, because ultralytics and transformers already cover those models.
recommendations: Free disk is no longer 5.7 GB. It read 5.7 GB at 03:00 KST, 29.7 GB at 03:09 and 43.3 GB (df avail) from 03:11 to 03:14 on 2026-11-25. The Trash (18.8 GB) was emptied and roughly 19 GB more was freed elsewhere during the probe, not by this probe. Re-check with df before installing; if it holds, both the lean (about 2.8 GB) and full (about 10.7 GB) budgets fit with the 10 GB reserve.

Memory is the tighter constraint. Swap was 10.2 GB used of 11.3 GB during the probe, in 11 one-gigabyte swap files that share the same APFS container as the data volume. Keep one model loaded at a time, and treat SAM 2.1 large, Grounding DINO base and SAM 3 as high risk on this 16 GB machine.

Pin to the cached versions. A ready constraints file is at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-limgiheon-Desktop-----capstone4-2/448b323c-cfea-4a04-b49e-4f432d2baf4f/scratchpad/probe/cache-constraints-py312.txt, and resolved candidate lists are L-pin-py312-mac15.txt (lean) and F-pin-py312-mac15.txt (full) in the same folder. The scratchpad can be cleared by a reboot, so copy them into the project if they will be used.
Do not run uv cache clean or uv cache prune before the lab environment exists; the cache is what makes the install nearly free.

The literal dry-run flags understate what this Mac gets. uv's --python-platform aarch64-apple-darwin assumes macOS 13.0, which hides torch 2.15.0 (macosx_14_0 wheels) and resolves torch 2.11.0, av 15.1.0 and OpenCV 5.0.0.93. A normal install on this Mac (macOS 15.7.9), or a resolve with MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0, gives torch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, av 19.0.2 and OpenCV 5.1.0.95.

OpenCV resolves to major version 5 (5.1.0.95) because ultralytics has no upper bound. If any classical pipeline depends on 4.x behaviour, pin opencv-python below 5; no 4.x opencv-python wheel is cached, so that costs a download of roughly 25-40 MB.

YOLOE text prompts need more than the model file: the mobileclip2_b.ts text encoder (242 MB) and the clip package from git+https://github.com/ultralytics/CLIP.git, which Ultralytics otherwise installs by itself at first use. Declare clip as a dependency so nothing is installed at run time. The prompt-free variants (yoloe-26s-seg-pf.pt, 38.1 MB) need neither.

SAM 3 is not practical before the competition: both facebook/sam3 and facebook/sam3.1 are gated with manual approval, no Hugging Face token is configured, the weights are 3.3 GB, and through Ultralytics it also needs clip and timm.

For Grounding DINO, OWLv2 and SAM 2.1 through transformers, load with from_pretrained, which fetches model.safetensors only. Downloading whole repositories doubles the size because they also hold pytorch_model.bin (Grounding DINO tiny 657 MB versus 1318 MB).

Put every model cache under one app data folder so the lab can show and delete them: set HF_HOME for Hugging Face, RF_HOME for RF-DETR (default /Users/limgiheon/.roboflow/models, which already has detection nano and small), and pass absolute paths for Ultralytics weights.

The existing Ultralytics settings at /Users/limgiheon/Library/Application Support/Ultralytics/settings.json have a relative weights_dir ("weights") and a datasets_dir pointing into the other project. Downloads would land relative to whatever the working directory is. Give the lab its own settings folder with YOLO_CONFIG_DIR rather than editing that file.

Write result videos with PyAV (the cached av 19.0.2 wheel bundles libx264) or the system ffmpeg (libx264 and h264_videotoolbox are present). The FFmpeg bundled inside the OpenCV wheel has no libx264, so cv2.VideoWriter output may not play in a browser. I did not test an actual encode.

If more disk is ever needed, the low-risk re-downloadable items add up to about 10 GB: npm cache 2.9 GB, Chrome cache 2.75 GB, VS Code updater staging 1.6 GB, pip cache 1.1 GB, JetBrains caches 0.7 GB, old Playwright Chromium revision 0.55 GB, Homebrew cleanup 0.5 GB. Larger but needing the user's decision: Docker disk image 21.7 GB, Downloads 18.4 GB, the other project's Hugging Face models 2.75 GB.
Have the app check free disk itself: warn below 10 GB and refuse uploads and runs below 5 GB.

All sizes are in MiB (bytes / 1,048,576). Weight sizes come from live HTTP headers and the Hugging Face API on 2026-11-25; package sizes come from PyPI wheel sizes, with unpacked sizes read from each wheel's file listing rather than a multiplier. The frontend, bytecode, clip, app-data and fine-tuning rows in the budget are estimates.
Nothing was installed, deleted or downloaded as weights. The probe used a private uv cache (about 40 MB) inside the probe folder; the whole probe folder is 42 MB.
